REGINA ONGSIAKO REYES Representative Lone District, Marinduque House of Representatives Batasan Hills, Quezon City Dear Hon. Reyes: This has reference to your letter dated 26 August 2014, vhich we received on 03 September 2014, seeking the Department's assistance in the form Of a legal opinion to determine who is authorized to occupy the vacant position in the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Buenavista, Marinduque, caused by the untimely demise of Vice-Mayor Montano P. Suguid (Vice-Mayor Suguid). Attached to your letter was Resolution No. 90-2014 entitled "RESOLUTION RESPECrFULLY REQUESTING FROM THE CHIEF OF LEGAL DEPARTMENT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT, REGIONAL OFFICE IV-B, NITY. OFELIO A. TACTAC JR. THRU THE REGIONAL DIRECTOR, ENGR. JAMES F. FADRILAN, REGION IV-B MIMAROPA TO RENDER LEGAL OPINION AND/OR INTERPRETATION IN THE DETERMINATION OF VACANT POSITION' AS STIPULATED IN SEC. 45 (B) OF RA 7160" adopted by the SB of Buenavista, Marinduque, on 18 August 2014. Per your letter and its attachments, Vice-Mayor Suguid, who was elected as such under the Liberal Party (LP), died. Liberal Party Provincial Chair, Governor Carmencita O. Reyes endorsed fellow LP Member Evelio S. Rosas to occupy the vacant SB seat. However, there are two (2) other contending appointees from two (2) different parties who both claim to hold the required certification and nomination. For this, the SB resolved to bring the matter to the Department. Hence, your letter cum indorsement. Per the Certified List of Elected Municipal Candidates with Party Affiliation and Votes Obtained in the last 13 May 2013 Synchronized National and Local Elections available in our records, hereunder is the list of municipal elective officials in Buenavista, Marinduque according to their ranking: Mayor Vice-Mayor SB Members Russel S. Madrigal Montano P. Suguid (NUP) (LP) (NUP) 1. 2. 3. 4. Bert S. Fabrero Eduardo L. Pampola (NUP) David G. Vitto (IND) Florentino B. Pinaroc (NUP) > I iq q: 10

Salvacion (LP) Per Section 44 (a)l of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 , the first-ranking SB Member (Bert S Fabrero) shall become the vice-mayor in view of the death of the elected Vice-Mayor, Montano P. Suguid. Subsequent vacancies in the SB shall be filled automatically by other sanggunian members according to their ranking. After applying such rule of automatic succession, there will be a resultant vacancy, specifically the eighth ranking member in the SB of that municipality. Said eighth place vacancy in the SB shall be filled up by appointment to be issued by the Governor pursuant to Section 45 (a) (2) and (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991. As to which political party will such appointee come from, the Department finds the Decision promulgated by the Supreme Court in G. R. No. 173165 entitled "Atty. Lucky M. Damasen vs. Oscar G. Tumamao"2 (Tumamao case) applicable. In this case, Nelia Tumamao, the Vice-Mayor of San Isidro, Isabela, died. As a result, a permanent vacancy was created in the Office of the Vice-Mayor. Pursuant to Section 44 of the Local Government Code of 1991, Ligaya C. Alonzo was elevated to the position of Vice-Mayor, she being the highest-ranking member of the SB, that is, the one who garnered the highest number of votes for that office. As a result, a permanent vacancy was created in the SB. To fill-up the ensuing vacancy in the SB, San Isidro Mayor Abraham T. Lim recommended to Governor Maria Gracia Cielo M. Padaca, the appointment of respondent Oscar G. Tamamao, a member of the Laban ng Demokratikong Pilipino (LDP), the same political party to which Alonzo belonged. Thereafter, Tumamao took his oath as a member of the SB and attended the regular session of the aforesaid August Body. Meantime, Atty. Lucky Damasen was able to secure from LDP Provincial Chairman Ana Benita Balauag a letter of nomination for his appointment to the SB. Atty. Damasen was also appointed by Governor Padaca and accordingly attended the SB sessions. The Supreme Court threshed the issue on who between Damasen and Tumamao is entitled to the contested position in this wise: "It is undisputed that the law applicable to herein petition is Sec. 45(b) of RA 7160, which provides for the rule on succession in cases of permanent vacancies in the Sanggunian, to wit: I Section 44. Permanent Vacancies in the Offices of the Governor, Vice-Governor, Mayor, and Vice-IWayor. - If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the governor or mayor, the vice-governor or vice-mayor concerned shall become the governor or mayor. If a permanent vacancy occurs in the offices of the governor, vice•-governor, mayor, or vice-mayor, the highest ranking sanggunian member or, in case Of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall become the governor, vice-governor, mayor or vice-mayor, as the case may be. Subsequent vacancies in the said office shall be filled automatically by the other sanggunian members according to their ranking as defined herein. 2 G.R. No.173165, 17 February 2010.

Section 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian. — (a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automatic succession provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: (1) The President, through the Executive Secretary, in the case of' the Sangguniang Panlala wigan and the Sangguniang Panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities; (2) The governor, in the case of the Sangguniang panlungsod of component cities and the Sangguniang Bayan; (3) The city or municipal mayor, in the case of Sangguniang Barangay, upon recommendation of the Sangguniang Barangay concerned (b) Except for the Sangguniang Barangay, only the nominee of the political party under which the sanggunian member concerned had been elected and whose elevation to theposition next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinabove provided. The appointee shall come from the same political party as that of' the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term OT the vacant office. In the appointment herein mentioned, a nomination and a certificate of membership of the appointee Trom thc highest official of the political party concerned are conditions sine qua non, and any appointment without such nomination and certification shall be null and void ab initio and shall be a ground for administrative action against the official responsible therefore.IW1 As can be gleaned from the above provision. the law provides Tor f uc sionta 1 First thea int hallcomc• from the same political party as that of the Sanggunian member who caused the vacancy, Second, the appointee must have a nomination and a erti/ic te OT Membersh from the Ili hest official OT the litical art concerned. In resolving the petition at bar, this Court is guided by Navarro v. Court of Appeals (Navarro), where this Court explained the reason behind the rule of succession under Sec. 45 (b) of RA 7160, to wit: The reason behind the right given to a political party to nominate a replacement where a permanent vacancy occurs in the Sanggunian is to maintain theparty representation as willed by the people in the election.

With the elevation of petitioner Tamayo, who belonged to REFORMA-LM, to the position of Vice-Mayor, a vacancy occurred ill the Sanggunian that should be filled up with someone belonging to the political party of petitioner Tamayo. Otherwise, REFORMA- IM's representation in the Sanggunian vvould be diminished. xxx. As earlier-pointed out, the reason behind Par. (b), Sec. 45 or Lhe Local Government Code is the maintenance of party representation in the Sanggunian in accordance with the will of the electorate. " n t the LDP representation. " (Emphasis Supplied) Applying the Supreme Court ruling in the Tumamao case to the case at hand, the person to be appointed to the resultant vacancy in the SB should come from the party of 1st-ranking SB Member, Bert S. Fabrero, which is NUP, not from LP which is the party affiliation of the deceased Vice-Mayor Saguid. Per the Navarro case, as reiterated in the Tumamao case, the elevation of 1 st-ranking SB Member Fabrero, who belonged to NIJP, to the position of Vice-Mayor, created the last vacancy in the SB that should be filled up with someone belonging to the political party of 1st-ranking SB Member Fabrero. Otherwise, NUP's representation in the SB would be diminished. Further, such appointee from the political party of 1st-ranking SB Member Fabrero must have a nomination and a Certificate of Membership from the highest official of the NUP. The highest official of the NUP refers to the Party Chairman. hope to have guided you accordingly.
